Scan script sections for mixed content and nonconforming lines: $ python3 - <<'PY' import re p='/app/script.txt' lines=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines() sec=None sections={} order=[] for i,l in enumerate(lines,1):     m=re.match(r'^\[(.+?)\]\s*$',l.strip())     if m:         sec=m.group(1)         order.append(sec)         sections.setdefault(sec,[])         continue     if sec is not None:         sections[sec].append((i,l))  # find sections that have both speaker lines and numbered choices mixed=[] for sec,content in sections.items():     non=[(i,l.strip()) for i,l in content if l.strip()]     has_choice=any(re.match(r'^\d+\.',t) for _,t in non)     has_speaker=any(re.match(r'^[^\[]+?:',t) for _,t in non)     if has_choice and has_speaker:         mixed.append(sec)  print('sections',len(sections)) print('mixed',mixed[:20], 'count',len(mixed)) # find lines not matching either speaker-with-arrow or choice-with-arrow bad=[] for sec,content in sections.items():     for i,l in content:         t=l.strip()         if not t: continue         if re.match(r'^\d+\..*->\s*\w+',t):             continue         if re.match(r'^[^:]+:.*->\s*\w+',t):             continue         # allow lines without -> ? none expected         bad.append((i,sec,t))  print('nonconforming lines',len(bad)) print('\n'.join(f'{i} [{sec}] {t}' for i,sec,t in bad[:30])) PY
Check if End section exists and where referenced: $ grep -n '^\[End\]' -n /app/script.txt || true; grep -n '-> End' /app/script.txt | head
Check existence of [End] section and its references: $ grep -n '^\[End\]' /app/script.txt || true; grep -n -- '-> End' /app/script.txt | head

Compute reachability and missing targets in script: $ python3 - <<'PY' import re, collections text=open('/app/script.txt',encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines() sections=[] sec=None content={} for l in text:     m=re.match(r'^\[(.+?)\]\s*$',l.strip())     if m:         sec=m.group(1)         sections.append(sec)         content[sec]=[]     elif sec is not None:         if l.strip():             content[sec].append(l.strip())  edges=[] for sec,lines in content.items():     for line in lines:         if '->' not in line: continue         left,right=[s.strip() for s in line.rsplit('->',1)]         target=right         edges.append((sec,target))  nodes=set(sections) # include End target if missing for _,t in edges:     if t not in nodes:         nodes.add(t)  start=sections[0] adj=collections.defaultdict(list) for a,b in edges:     adj[a].append(b)  seen=set([start]) q=collections.deque([start]) while q:     u=q.popleft()     for v in adj.get(u,[]):         if v not in seen:             seen.add(v)             q.append(v)  unreach=sorted(nodes-seen) print('start',start) print('nodes',len(nodes),'sections',len(sections),'edges',len(edges)) print('unreachable count',len(unreach)) print('first few',unreach[:20]) missing_targets=sorted({t for _,t in edges if t not in sections}) print('missing section for targets',missing_targets) PY

response:
Implemented `/app/solution.py` with `parse_script(text: str)` that parses the bracketed-section script format into a structured graph:

- Nodes: `{"id","text","speaker","type"}` where `type` is `"line"` or `"choice"`
- Edges: `{"from","to","text"}` where `text` is the option label for choice edges (and `""` for line transitions)

The parser also validates:
- all nodes are reachable from the first section (`[Start]`)
- all edge targets exist (it auto-creates an implicit `End` node if referenced)

Generated outputs (via running `python3 /app/solution.py`):
- `/app/dialogue.json` (205 nodes, 321 edges)
- `/app/dialogue.dot` (Graphviz DOT visualization)
